note: S80 separates the auth path from the answer set BEFORE measuring, because a single total would let the answer size decide a verdict about branching (A18). Counts and digests only, no timings.

controls.name: C_completeness_proofs_verify
controls.must_fire_because: a completeness proof that its own verifier rejects is a number about nothing, and this is the proof kind whose verifier is the anti-omission check -- W2 drives it to False with C_omit / C_add / C_tamper
controls.can_fail_because: any completeness proof fails verification, or any query fails to cover
controls.null_must_contain: W2's verify_completeness, which returns False on an omitted, added or tampered key and is free to reject every proof here

controls.name: C_auth_path_comparison_is_decisive
controls.must_fire_because: the falsifier here is an ORDERING, so what has to be checked is that the ordering was decidable at all: three sets, real verified proofs, and values far enough apart that the ranking is not noise
controls.can_fail_because: fewer than three sets produced proofs, or the largest and smallest auth-path means are within 5% of each other, making the ranking noise
controls.null_must_contain: auth-path values free to tie or to sit within rounding of each other, in which case no ordering claim could be made in either direction

controls.name: C_answer_size_is_a_separate_axis
controls.must_fire_because: if the answer set ordered the sets the same way the auth path does, a single total would be safe to publish and the separation this spike insists on would be decoration
controls.can_fail_because: the answer-size ordering matches the auth-path ordering, making the two axes indistinguishable on this corpus
controls.null_must_contain: answer sizes free to correlate with the auth path -- nothing in the construction forces the two orderings apart, and on a different corpus they could coincide

controls.name: C_queries_are_scale_matched
controls.must_fire_because: a query taken at a fixed BYTE depth sits near the root of a 1,155-byte atom key and near the leaf of a 12-byte triple key, which compares two regimes and calls it a comparison
controls.can_fail_because: mean query length is not close to FRACTION of mean key length for every set
controls.null_must_contain: the key lengths themselves, which differ by 90x across these sets and would produce wildly unmatched query depths under a fixed-byte rule
